title: Vegetable Broth
summary: A clean, aromatic vegetable stock — the base for the vegetable and wild-mushroom paellas. Makes about 3 liters. From a paella class at The Paella Club, Barcelona.
steps: Wash all of the vegetables.
Chop them all into medium-sized cubes.
Place a large deep pot over medium heat.
Fry the chopped vegetables until softened and browned, about 10 minutes.
Add the water and bring the mixture to a boil.
Turn the heat down to low and simmer for 30 minutes (use a timer).
Using a spider or handheld sieve, skim off any foam that appears on the surface.
Once the broth has simmered 30 minutes, strain out all of the vegetables.
Return the liquid to the stove and reduce over medium heat for a further 20 minutes, until reduced by about three-quarters.
Remove from the heat and let cool to room temperature.
Refrigerate.
Chef's tip: this broth freezes well and keeps up to 6 months.

title: Seafood Broth
summary: A rich shellfish stock built from crustacean shells and white fish — the base for the seafood and black-rice paellas. Makes about 3 liters. From a paella class at The Paella Club, Barcelona.
steps: Place a large deep pot over high heat.
Add the olive oil and brown the garlic cloves, leaving them whole.
Before the oil starts to smoke, add all of the crustacean shells and white fish, stirring well.
Turn the heat down to medium and, using the back of a wooden spoon, press down on the ingredients to release their flavor. Cook a further 5 minutes.
Add all of the water and bring the mixture to a boil.
Turn the heat down to low and simmer for 30 minutes (use a timer).
Using a spider or handheld sieve, skim off any foam that appears on the surface.
Strain out the ingredients, keeping only the liquid.
Reduce the liquid by half over a low simmer, about 20 minutes.
Season to taste. Remove from the heat and cool to room temperature, then refrigerate.
Chef's tip: this broth freezes well and keeps up to 6 months.

title: Beef Broth
summary: A deep roasted-bone stock — the meat broth for the pork/chicken paella. Makes about 3 liters. From a paella class at The Paella Club, Barcelona.
steps: Preheat the oven to 250°C / 480°F.
Roughly chop the carrots and celery into chunks.
Place all of the beef bones on a large baking tray and coat them with olive oil.
Roast the bones in the oven until golden brown and dark in color.
Transfer the roasted bones to a large deep pot, add the chopped carrots and celery, and pour in all of the water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer over medium heat for 30 minutes (use a timer).
Strain out the bones and discard.
Simmer the liquid over low heat a further 20 minutes, until reduced by about three-quarters.
Salt to taste.
Remove from the stove.
Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate.
Chef's tip: this broth freezes well and keeps up to 6 months.

title: Seafood Paella
summary: Shrimp and squid over saffron bomba rice with a slow-built sofrito and a crisp socarrat. Serves 2. From a paella class at The Paella Club, Barcelona.
ingredients: 120g rice, preferably bomba (or substitute any risotto rice)
steps: Set the paella pan over low/medium heat.
Generously drizzle in most of the olive oil, saving a quarter for later.
Add the whole garlic clove and the lemon rind and cook until both turn golden; remove both, setting the garlic clove aside for later.
Sear all of the shrimp for 30 seconds on each side.
Using the back of a wooden spoon, press firmly on the shrimp heads until all of the liquid (coral) is released, and let it caramelize in the pan, about 30 seconds.
Remove all of the shrimp to a plate.
Add a little more olive oil and cook the squid rings for about 30 seconds all over, then remove the squid and any juices to the same plate as the shrimp.
To begin the sofrito, add a little more olive oil, add the chopped onion, and fry until golden; meanwhile finely mince the reserved garlic clove and add it to the onion.
Once the onion and garlic reach the desired caramelization, set them aside in a corner of the pan.
Place the red peppers in the centre of the pan, add a drizzle of olive oil, and cook until charred, 8 to 10 minutes.
Mix all of the vegetables together and continue cooking until dark in colour, constantly moving them to distribute the heat evenly.
Deglaze the pan with the white wine; once the alcohol has evaporated, add the tomato puree and reduce until it reaches a jam-like texture.
To bloom the spices, make a small well in the centre, add a tbsp of olive oil and the saffron powder; when it bubbles, incorporate it well into the sauce.
Add all of the rice, mixing it fully into the sofrito, and cook in the sauce for a further 2 minutes.
Add all of the fish broth, mixing well and slowly so none is lost over the sides, and raise to a medium heat. Season to taste.

Stir in small circular motions around the pan, drawing into the centre and picking up anything stuck to the bottom. After about four minutes the mixture becomes thick and gelatinous — a sign the starch has been extracted; if not, stir another two minutes.
Remove the spoon and, holding the handles, keep the pan on the heat and shake slowly for about 60 seconds until the mixture is evenly spread across the pan.
To build the crisp socarrat, leave the pan over medium heat; smoke from the centre signals the rice is caramelizing — when it smells like burnt toast (about 2 minutes), turn off the heat.
Lay the seafood delicately on top of the rice — do not press it in or stir the rice — and add the reserved squid juices.
Cook the paella in the oven at 200°C / 395°F for 15 minutes.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve.

title: Wild Mushroom & Black Truffle Paella
summary: An earthy vegetarian paella — wild mushrooms and a caramelized carrot-and-onion sofrito over bomba rice, finished with black truffle oil. Serves 2. From a paella class at The Paella Club, Barcelona.
ingredients: 120g rice, preferably bomba (or substitute any risotto rice)
steps: Set the paella pan over low/medium heat.
Generously drizzle in most of the olive oil, saving a quarter for later.
Add the leek and sear until golden and softened.
Remove the leek and save for later.
To begin the sofrito, add a little more olive oil and the finely chopped carrot, spread evenly across the pan.
Cook the carrot until it shrinks, turns brown, and is crispy — about 4 to 6 minutes.
Remove the carrot, saving as much oil as possible.
Add the finely chopped onion and cook until golden.
Return the cooked carrot to the onion, mix well, and cook a further 2 minutes.
Move all of the ingredients to the side of the pan and add a drop of olive oil to the centre.
Place the wild mushrooms in the centre of the pan and cook for 2 minutes.
Mix all of the ingredients together.
Deglaze the pan with the red wine; once the alcohol has evaporated, add the tomato puree and reduce until it reaches a jam-like texture, about 2 minutes.
Add all of the rice, mixing it fully into the sofrito, and cook in the sauce for 2 minutes.
Add all of the vegetable broth, mixing well and slowly so none is lost over the sides, and raise to a medium heat. Season to taste.

Stir in small circular motions around the pan, drawing into the centre and picking up anything stuck to the bottom. After about four minutes the mixture becomes thick and gelatinous — a sign the starch has been extracted; if not, stir a further 2 minutes.
Remove the spoon and, holding the handles, keep the pan on the heat and shake slowly for about 60 seconds until the mixture is evenly spread across the pan.
To build the crisp socarrat, leave the pan over medium heat; when the smoke smells like burnt toast, turn off the heat.
Lay the seared leek delicately on top of the rice — do not press it in or stir the rice.
Cook the paella in the oven at 200°C / 395°F for 15 minutes.
Drizzle with truffle infused oil and serve.

title: Pork/Chicken & Spring Garlic Paella
summary: A meat paella — paprika-rubbed pork or chicken with spring garlic, wild mushrooms, and saffron over bomba rice. Serves 2. From a paella class at The Paella Club, Barcelona.
ingredients: Sprig of fresh rosemary, sage, or thyme
120g rice, preferably bomba (or substitute any risotto rice)
steps: Dry-rub the meat with ½ tsp of the salt and the sweet paprika; shake in a bag or bowl until well coated. Set aside.
Set the paella pan over low/medium heat.
Generously drizzle in most of the olive oil, saving a quarter for later.
Add the whole garlic clove and the herb sprig and cook until both turn golden; remove both, setting the garlic clove aside for later.
Sear the meat for 2 minutes on each side, then remove.
To begin the sofrito, add a little more olive oil, add the chopped onion, and fry until golden; meanwhile finely mince the reserved garlic clove and add it to the onion.
Once the onion and garlic reach the desired caramelization, set them aside in a corner of the pan.
Place the spring garlic in the centre of the pan, add a drizzle of olive oil, and cook until charred, 2 to 4 minutes.
Mix all of the vegetables together and continue cooking until dark in colour, constantly moving them to distribute the heat evenly.
Move all of the ingredients to the side of the pan and add a drop of olive oil to the centre.
Place the wild mushrooms in the centre of the pan and cook for 2 minutes.
Mix all of the ingredients together.
Deglaze the pan with the red wine; once the alcohol has evaporated, add the tomato puree and reduce until it reaches a jam-like texture, about 2 minutes.
To bloom the spices, make a small well in the centre, add a tbsp of olive oil and the saffron powder and remaining sweet paprika; when it bubbles, incorporate it into the sofrito.
Add all of the rice, mixing it fully into the sofrito, and cook in the sauce for 2 minutes.
Add all of the meat broth, mixing well and slowly so none is lost over the sides, and raise to a medium heat. Season to taste.

Stir in small circular motions around the pan, drawing into the centre and picking up anything stuck to the bottom. After about four minutes the mixture becomes thick and gelatinous — a sign the starch has been extracted; if not, stir another two minutes.
Remove the spoon and, holding the handles, keep the pan on the heat and shake slowly for about 60 seconds until the mixture is evenly spread across the pan.
To build the crisp socarrat, leave the pan over medium heat; when the smoke smells like burnt toast, turn off the heat.
Lay the meat delicately on top of the rice — do not press it in or stir the rice.
Cook the paella in the oven at 200°C / 395°F for 15 minutes.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve.
